sources.name: Kimi Help Center: Introducing Kimi Agent

caption:
Kimi is Moonshot AI's free assistant: pick a model, upload up to 50 files, or let its agent build slides, sheets and websites for you.
It searches the web on its own when a question needs it.
The full guide with 5 prompts is on neurafeedai.com.

Have you tried Kimi yet?

Follow @neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: Kimi Help Center · Photo: Kimi
threads_text: Kimi is the Chinese AI assistant most people in the US have not tried, and its free agent builds slides, spreadsheets and whole websites from one prompt. It also reads up to 50 files at once. Would you hand your work files to a chatbot from Beijing?

slides.headline: How to use *Kimi AI*, the free assistant that builds your slides

slides.heading: 1. Pick your *model*
paras: Use the switch above the input box. K2.6 is fast, K3 is the most capable, K3 Swarm runs big searches.
Kimi decides by itself when to search the web.

slides.heading: 2. Drop in your *files*
paras: PDF, Word, Excel, slides, images, text and video. Up to 100 MB each, up to 50 files.
Ask it to quote the passage behind every answer.

slides.heading: 3. Hand big jobs to the *Agent*
paras: Open kimi.com/agent and describe the whole task: a deck, a cleaned spreadsheet, a website.
You can watch every step, then download the file.

slides.heading: 4. Get *finished files* back
paras: Word, PDF, Excel, slides, charts or a live web page you can share.
Check numbers before you send anything it made.

slides.hook: Follow for guides to the AI tools your feed is not talking about yet.

site_article.headline: How to use Kimi AI: models, files, Agent and 5 prompts
site_article.dek: A practical walkthrough of Moonshot AI's assistant: which model to pick, how file uploads work, how to hand tasks to Kimi Agent, and what the help center leaves out.
site_article.summary: Kimi is Moonshot AI's assistant, available at kimi.com and in mobile apps, with models picked from a switch above the input box. It reads up to 50 files of up to 100 MB each, and its agent turns one prompt into slides, documents, spreadsheets or a web page.

site_article.answer_summary: Open kimi.com or the Kimi app, choose a model with the switch above the input box and type your request. Upload files for long documents, and use Kimi Agent at kimi.com/agent when you want slides, sheets, documents or a website made for you.
site_article.hero_alt: Screenshot of the Kimi web app from Kimi's help center.

paragraphs.text: Kimi is an AI assistant built by Moonshot AI, a Beijing company founded in 2023. If you want to know how to use Kimi AI, the short version is this: open kimi.com or the Kimi app, pick a model with the switch above the input box, and type. Kimi decides on its own when to search the web, reads long files, and can hand bigger jobs to an agent that builds slides, documents, spreadsheets and websites.

Kimi gets less attention in the US than ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini, but its agent tools are some of the most complete in any free chat app. This guide covers where to start, which model to pick, how to work with files, and when to switch to the agent. It also says plainly what the help center does not tell you.
How to use Kimi AI: getting started

paragraphs.title: 1. Open Kimi on the web or on your phone
paragraphs.text: Kimi runs in the browser at kimi.com with nothing to install. There is also a mobile app for iOS and Android (and HarmonyOS), and Kimi's help center links a desktop download for Mac. Wikipedia lists kimi.com for mainland China and kimi.ai as the international site; both lead to the same assistant.

paragraphs.title: 2. Pick a model with the switch above the input box
paragraphs.text: Kimi's help center says you change models with the model switch button above the input box. The current lineup is K2.6 for fast conversation and quick answers, K3, which Kimi calls its most capable model for chat and agent tasks, and K3 Swarm for large search and batch jobs. K2.6 offers Standard or High thinking strength; K3 and K3 Swarm offer Low, High or Max.

Start with K2.6 for quick questions. Switch to K3 when the task needs real reasoning, and save K3 Swarm for jobs where you want many sources searched at once. Higher thinking strength usually means a slower answer, so do not leave it on Max for small talk.

paragraphs.title: 3. Just ask, and let Kimi decide when to search
paragraphs.text: There is no search toggle. According to the help center, Kimi decides by itself whether a question needs a web search. If you want fresh information, say so in the prompt, for example by naming a date or asking for current sources.

paragraphs.title: Prompt 1: Get a sourced answer on something recent
paragraphs.text: Search the web for news from the last 7 days about [topic]. Give me the 5 most important developments, one sentence each, with the source and date for every point. Flag anything that only one source reports.
Working with files in Kimi

paragraphs.title: 4. Upload documents, sheets, images or video
paragraphs.text: Kimi reads PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, images, TXT files and video. The help center gives a limit of 100 MB per file and up to 50 files in a session. Long context is Kimi's oldest strength: the first public version in 2023 already handled 128,000 tokens, and Kimi says K3 has a 1 million token context window.

paragraphs.title: Prompt 2: Compare two long documents
paragraphs.text: I uploaded two versions of the same contract. List every clause that changed between version 1 and version 2. For each change, quote the old and new wording and explain in one sentence what it means for [me / my company].
Ask Kimi to quote the exact passage behind each answer when you work with a long file. It makes mistakes easy to spot, and you can jump straight to the page to check.

paragraphs.title: 5. Save prompts you reuse
paragraphs.text: Kimi lets you store prompts you use often. The help center calls them Presets on one page and Quick prompts on another. Save the ones you type every week, like a meeting summary format or a translation style.

paragraphs.title: 6. Turn on Memory if you want Kimi to remember you
paragraphs.text: With Memory switched on, Kimi can refer to its Memory Space and to your past chats when it answers. You manage what it keeps in the settings. Leave it off if you share the account or do not want past chats used.
How to use Kimi Agent for bigger jobs

Kimi Agent is the part that does the work instead of chatting about it. Kimi says it plans a task, uses more than 20 built-in tools, including code, a terminal, a browser and image and audio generation, and hands back finished files. It grew out of OK Computer, the agent mode Kimi launched in September 2025.

paragraphs.title: 7. Open the agent and describe the task
paragraphs.text: On the web, the agent lives at kimi.com/agent. In the app, Kimi's instructions are to pick K3 or K3 Swarm in the model switch above the chat box. Then describe the whole task in one message, including what you want delivered and in which format.

paragraphs.title: 8. Watch the work, then download the result
paragraphs.text: While the agent runs, you can follow its reasoning, the tools it calls, the websites it visits and the intermediate steps. When it finishes you get the deliverable: a code project, Word, PDF or Markdown documents, Excel or CSV sheets, slides, charts, or a deployed web page you can preview, download or share.

paragraphs.title: Prompt 3: Turn a report into a slide deck
paragraphs.text: Turn the PDF I uploaded into a 12 slide presentation for [audience]. One idea per slide, a short title, no more than 3 bullet points each, and a final slide with the 3 main takeaways. Deliver it as an editable PPT file.

paragraphs.title: Prompt 4: Clean up a messy spreadsheet
paragraphs.text: In the Excel file I uploaded, remove duplicate rows, fix the date column so every date uses the same format, and add a summary sheet with totals by [category] and a chart of the monthly trend. Return a new Excel file and tell me what you changed.

paragraphs.title: 9. Use Deep Research for a long report
paragraphs.text: Deep Research is one of the agent's modes. Kimi describes it as long-form research with complex search, multi-step reasoning and charts, and its help center has a prompt library sorted by use: industry research, competitor analysis, due diligence, legal research, academic work, policy and personal decisions.

paragraphs.title: Prompt 5: Research before a big purchase
paragraphs.text: Research [product category] for someone who [your situation]. Compare the 5 best options on price, reliability, and what owners complain about most. End with a clear recommendation and the 3 sources you trusted most.

For heavier jobs, Kimi also lists Agent Swarm, which it says can coordinate up to 300 sub-agents and more than 4,000 tool calls, Kimi Code, a command line tool and VS Code extension for programmers, Kimi Claw, a cloud agent it says starts in under 30 seconds, and Kimi Work, a desktop agent for Mac and Windows.
What Kimi costs and where it falls short

According to Wikipedia, the Kimi apps are free with general rate limits, and paid plans named Moderato, Allegro, Allegretto and Vivace raise those limits and speed up agent tasks. The help pages used for this guide do not list prices, so check the membership page inside Kimi before you pay. Deep Research tasks use credits, according to Kimi's own FAQ list.

Two things to know before you trust it with work data. Moonshot AI is based in Beijing, so read the privacy terms with that in mind. And Kimi K3 has faced accusations, including from the director of the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy, that it was built by distilling Anthropic's Claude, according to Wikipedia.

Kimi is a strong pick for long documents, slides and spreadsheet work, and its agent is generous for a free app. Like every chatbot, it can be confidently wrong, so check numbers and quotes against the source before you send anything Kimi made.
